focus_register_connective.relaxed_rule: c01-t12: accept "That's true/You're right, but" (literal 그렇기는 한데); c02-t12: accept any rendering addressed to the listener as "you" even with a vocative title (Team Leader/Manager/boss); c02-t15: accept "But" as topic shift; c05-t14: accept vocative "Oppa". c03-t14, c04-t12 unchanged.

diagnosis.c01-t12: check wording: the check explicitly fails the literal, natural rendering "That's true, but I was still late" (Korean 그렇기는 한데 itself concedes). 59/60 main+baseline+s1 rows fail on this wording alone; judge applies it faithfully.
diagnosis.c02-t15: check strict: "But" as a spoken topic-shift is marginal English; judge follows the check. All Qwen and most Gemma fail only on this.
diagnosis.c04-t12: real model error for "Then/Well then" (Qwen, Gemma, DeepL). Judge is stricter than the check on "Okay"/"Yeah" (4 of 22 verdicts I would pass).
diagnosis.c02-t12: check strict: vocative "Team Leader/Manager" fails even when the question is addressed to "you"; only third-person renderings are real errors (also caught by the pronoun check).
diagnosis.c03-t14: real error: "Mom"/"Grandma"/"Doctor" for 어머님; judge correct.
diagnosis.c05-t14: mostly real (brother/"my brother"); vocative "Oppa" (gpt-6-luna, 7 of 15 rows) fails only because of wording.
